opening.quote: Good afternoon, tide well Home, my is Sanne. How can I help?
opening.comment: You greeted the caller and gave the company name, but your own name was garbled in the transcript; a clear 'my name is Sanne at Tidewell Home' would be ideal, though the greeting itself meets the standard.

verification.quote: Can I take your full name and your order number or postcode, please?
verification.comment: You asked for the full name and order number before discussing the order, and the caller supplied both, which is correct.

understanding.quote: I returned a pair of curtains and I'm wondering where my refund is.
understanding.comment: You correctly captured the issue (refund for returned curtains) without asking for information the caller had already given.

resolution_accuracy.quote: Refunds are paid within 5 working days of the return arriving, so it will be on your card within 5 working days from yesterday.
resolution_accuracy.comment: The policy says the refund is paid within 5 working days of arrival, but the bank showing it can take longer; saying it will be on the card within 5 working days overstates the timeline, so be precise about when it is paid versus when it appears on the card.

process_compliance.quote: Can I put you on hold for a moment while I check the refund is queued?
process_compliance.comment: You asked permission before the hold and thanked the caller on return, which meets the requirement; no damaged-item or bank-dispute step applied.

communication.quote: Thank you for waiting. It's queued, and you'll get ans email the day it's paid.
communication.comment: The caller was polite and not frustrated, so no acknowledgement was needed, and your tone was courteous throughout.

closing.quote: Is there anything else I can help you with?
closing.comment: You confirmed the next step (email when paid), asked if there was anything else, and closed politely by thanking the caller.
